text: Richard Meier, born October 12, 1934, is an American abstract artist and architect known for his geometric designs that prominently feature the color white. A recipient of the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1984, Meier has designed several iconic buildings, including the Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art, the Getty Center in Los Angeles (completed 1997), the High Museum of Art in Atlanta (completed 1983), and San Jose City Hall (completed 2005). He was born to a Jewish family in Newark, New Jersey, the oldest of three sons of Carolyn (Kaltenbacher) and Jerome Meier, a wholesale wine and liquor salesman, and grew up in nearby Maplewood, where he attended Columbia High School. Meier earned a Bachelor of Architecture degree from Cornell University in 1957. After graduation, he traveled to Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Israel, and Italy to network with architects. He worked briefly in 1959 for Skidmore, Owings and Merrill and then for three years with Marcel Breuer before founding his own firm in 1963. In 1972, Meier was identified as one of The New York Five, a group of modernist architects alongside Peter Eisenman, Michael Graves, Charles Gwathmey, and John Hejduk. Early in his career, he worked with artist Frank Stella and favored white, geometric structures. Meier gained recognition for his designs of various houses, The Atheneum (completed 1979), and the High Museum of Art in Atlanta. His design for the Getty Center brought him widespread acclaim. Other notable commissions from this period include the Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art (completed 1995), the Paley Center for Media (completed 1996), The Hague City Hall (completed 1995), San Jose City Hall (completed 2005), the reconstruction of City Tower in Prague (completed 2008), and residential projects such as 173 and 176 Perry Street in Manhattan (completed 2002) and Meier on Rothschild in Tel Aviv (completed 2015). MeierPartners has offices in New York and Los Angeles, with projects in China, Tel Aviv, Paris, and Hamburg. Much of Meier's work is influenced by early to mid-20th-century architects, especially Le Corbusier, particularly his early works like the Villa Savoye and the Swiss Pavilion; Meier is considered to have implemented more of Corbusier's ideas than anyone, including Corbusier himself. His work also reflects influences from Mies Van der Rohe, Frank Lloyd Wright, and Luis Barragán (without color). White has been used in historical architectural landmarks such as cathedrals and white-washed villages in Spain, southern Italy, and Greece. In 2013, the Mayor of Rome, Gianni Alemanno, promised to remove the large travertine wall of Meier's Museum of the Ara Pacis, agreeing to reduce its height between an open-air space and a road along the Tiber River, with plans to build a wide pedestrian area and run the road underneath. Meier supported the plan, stating that the wall was originally built for traffic and noise, and that opening the piazza to the river would be beneficial. The mayor's office stated the project was intended to be completed by the end of his term in 2013, but the underpass project has not progressed and remained unchanged by 2024. In 1984, Meier received the Pritzker Prize, with the jury citing his "personal, vigorous, original" structures. In 2008, he won the gold medal from the Academy of Arts and Letters, and his project Jesolo Lido Village received the Dedalo Minosse International Prize. Meier is a Senior Fellow of the Design Futures Council and received the AIA Gold Medal in 1997 and the A+ Lifetime Achievement Award in 2013. He also received the Golden Plate Award in 1996 and in 2010, Cornell University established a professorship named for him. In 2014, Meier opened a 15,000-square-foot exhibition space at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City, which gathers much of his life's work, including his sculptures, architectural drawings, and collages, for the first time, and includes a planned research library. This replaced a smaller venue in Long Island City, Queens, which was open only by appointment to students and tour groups until 2013. On March 13, 2018, The New York Times reported allegations from women that Meier had sexually harassed or assaulted them; Meier responded by taking a six-month leave from his firm. In response, Cornell University declined his intended endowment and reviewed his previous donations. On April 6, 2018, four additional women who had worked at his firm came forward with allegations, some dating to 2009. On October 9, 2018, the firm announced that Meier's resignation was permanent. Major works by Meier include the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, the Barcelona Museum of Contemporary Art, the Getty Center, Meier on Rothschild, and On Prospect Park.
